text: Balar Malar Parramatta - Staff and Student Code of Conduct

title: Code Of_conduct
text: 1. Staff & Volunteer Information Handling Protocol: - Device Security: Staff must access the portal using personal, password-protected user accounts. Shared accounts are strictly prohibited. Always log out when using public/shared computers. - No Downloading PII: Staff should never download raw student/parent spreadsheets containing phone numbers, emails, or DOBs to their personal local hard drives. Access records directly through the secure portal interface. - Printed attendance logs or registration sheets must not be left unattended in classrooms. Shred or securely dispose of printouts at the end of the term. - WWC Checks: Only verified administrators can approve and verify Working With Children status. - Email Safety: When emailing multiple parents, staff must use BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) to prevent exposing email addresses in bulk mailouts.

title: Code Of_conduct
text: 2. Student Guidelines and Discipline: - Punctuality: Students must arrive 10 minutes before class starts. - Language: Students are encouraged to communicate primarily in Tamil during school hours. - Mobile Devices: Mobile phones must be turned off or kept on silent in school bags during lessons. - Respect: Bullying, harassment, or disrespectful behavior towards teachers, volunteers, or fellow students will not be tolerated and may lead to suspension. - Cleanliness: Students are responsible for maintaining classroom cleanliness and disposing of waste in recycling/general waste bins. - Pick-up Safety: Parents must sign students out at the designated pick-up zones. Students are not allowed to leave the premises unaccompanied unless written authorization is provided.

title: Curriculum Guide
text:
Balar Malar Parramatta - School Curriculum Guide (KG to Year 9)
1. Kindergarten (KG) & Year 1 (Primary Literacy): - Goal: Familiarize children with basic Tamil sounds, spoken vocabulary, and alphabet recognition. - Content: Tamil Vowels (உயிரெழுத்துக்கள் - 12 letters) and Tamil Consonants (மெய்யெழுத்துக்கள் - 18 letters). - Focus: Simple coloring workbooks, singing Tamil kids rhymes (e.g. நிலா நிலா ஓடி வா), identifying animals, colors, and fruits in Tamil. - Expected Outcome: Ability to read and write all 30 primary letters and speak short sentences.

title: Curriculum Guide
text: 2. Year 2 & Year 3 (Word Building & Alphabetic Writing): - Goal: Learn letter combinations, reading short paragraphs, and simple moral values. - Content: Ayutha Ezhuthu (ஃ), building Tamil words combining consonants and vowels (உயிர்மெய் எழுத்துக்கள்). - Focus: Introduction to Athichudi (ஆத்திசூடி) verses by Avvaiyar with meanings. - Expected Outcome: Ability to read simple stories, write spelling lists, and comprehend short stories (like Panchatantra fables).

title: Curriculum Guide
text: 3. Year 4 & Year 5 (Intermediate Grammar & Sentences): - Goal: Structure sentences, differentiate noun/verb classes, and write short paragraphs. - Content: Parts of speech (பெயர்ச்சொல், வினைச்சொல்), tenses (இறந்த காலம், நிகழ்காலம், எதிர்காலம்). - Focus: Studying Thirukkural (திருக்குறள்) verses with moral stories. - Expected Outcome: Writing weekly diary entries, constructing grammatically correct questions, and reading children's books independently.

title: Curriculum Guide
text: 4. Year 6 & Year 7 (Literature & Conversational Tamil): - Goal: Vocabulary extension, public speaking, and understanding Tamil history. - Content: Tales of Tenali Raman, Sangam Literature fables adapted for children, and historical essays. - Focus: Writing structured paragraphs, advanced verbs, and participating in debates. - Expected Outcome: Delivering a 2-minute speech in Tamil, reading complex storybooks, and writing descriptive essays.

title: Curriculum Guide
text: 5. Year 8 & Year 9 (Advanced Prose & Cultural Studies): - Goal: Literary appreciation, advanced grammar conventions, and Tamil heritage. - Content: Ancient Tamil dynasties (Chera, Chola, Pandya), trade routes, temple architectures, and formal essay writing. - Focus: Reading Tamil prose, writing multi-paragraph reports, and active participation in school newsletters. - Expected Outcome: Structuring research papers in Tamil, reading news prints, and translating complex English passages to Tamil.

title: Privacy Policy
text: Balar Malar Parramatta Data Privacy and Compliance Policy

title: Privacy Policy
text: 1. What Information We Collect: We collect personal information necessary to safely run school classes and manage enrollments: - Student Details: Full Name, Tamil Name, Date of Birth, Gender, Mainstream School/Grade, and Class Enrollment. - Parent/Guardian Details: Names, Email Addresses, Mobile Phone Numbers, and Volunteer preferences. - Staff/Volunteer Details: Names, Contact Details, Working With Children (WWC) check numbers, verification status, and signatures. - Attendance & Academic Reports: Attendance records, homework records, and term report card grades.

title: Privacy Policy
text: 2. Why We Collect It: We collect and use this information to: - Manage student enrollments and class allocations. - Keep attendance sheets for safety and child protection requirements. - Communicate with parents regarding class announcements or emergencies. - Issue academic report cards and school books/materials.

title: Privacy Policy
text:
3. How We Store and Protect Your Data: - All data is stored securely in Google Cloud Firestore (Sydney Region) using secure token-based encryption. - Only authorized staff members (Admins, class Teachers) can access contact details or student records. - We do not sell, rent, or share personal data with third-party advertisers or external organisations.
4. Accessing or Correcting Your Data: Parents have the right to request access to, or correction of, the personal information we hold about them or their children. Requests can be sent via email to the School Administrator.

title: Privacy Policy
text: 5. Data Breach Response Plan (IT & Admin Team): - Step 1: Containment. Identify the source of the breach and isolate it to prevent further data exposure. Revoke active tokens in Firebase Console, rotate database secrets, or disable compromised accounts. - Step 2: Assessment. Within 24 Hours, assess what data was exposed and determine if the breach is likely to result in serious harm (identity theft, harassment, or child safety risks). - Step 3: Notification. Within 72 Hours, send a clear notification email to affected parents/volunteers. Describe what happened, what data was involved, and recommended actions they should take. Report eligible data breaches to the OAIC under Australian law if required. - Step 4: Prevention. Review database security rules, security logs, and user authorization claims to prevent recurrence.
